chunks: "I'd first check which direction you mean, because literally 'increase the rise time' is making it slower.
I'll assume you mean the common case: the rising edge is too slow and I want to speed it up, meaning shorten the rise time. And I'll mention how to do the opposite at the end.
The rise time is set by the pull-up charging the bus capacitance, about 0. 85 times R p times C b . So I have three levers.
One, lower the pull-up resistance: halving it halves the rise time, but I'm limited by how much current the weakest device can sink, so R p can't go below (V DD-V OL) over I OL , about 970 ohms at 3.
3 volts. Two, reduce the bus capacitance: shorten traces and cables, remove devices or low-capacitance protection parts, or put branches behind a mux.

Three, if the resistor window is already closed, change the architecture: use a bus buffer with a rise-time accelerator, a current-source pull-up, or drop to a slower speed mode that allows a longer rise time.
If I actually wanted a slower edge, for example to cut ringing or EMI on a short, lightly loaded bus, I'd do the opposite: a bigger resistor, or a small series resistor and capacitor at the driver."
